note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: 4-day history of upper-respiratory symptoms after close contact with a sneezing coworker (possible viral exposure).
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Day 1–2: Sudden sore throat with odynophagia, low-grade fever, runny nose (clear discharge), nasal congestion.  
  • Day 3–4: Sore throat improving; new persistent dry cough; continued nasal congestion; night sweats; fatigue; generalized headaches and myalgias; low-grade fever now resolved with OTC antipyretics.  
- ENT symptoms:  
  • Throat: initial pain on swallowing; no current throat tightness, voice change, dysphagia, drooling, or visible lesions reported.  
  • Nose: clear rhinorrhea, significant congestion.  
  • Ears: no otalgia, no discharge, no fullness/hearing change.  
  • Airway/respiratory: mild exertional dyspnea; none at rest; no stridor/noisy breathing.  
  • No facial/lip/tongue swelling, no neck pain/swelling.  
- Relevant past episodes/treatment: None similar; self-treated with paracetamol and ibuprofen (doses/frequency not documented). No prior ED visits or epinephrine use.
- Allergies: Denies medication or food allergies.
- Current medications: Paracetamol PRN – dose/route not documented. Ibuprofen PRN – dose/route not documented.
- Social context: Lives alone; working as an accountant; occasional cigar smoker; social alcohol intake; able to self-care.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: None reported.
- Airway/breathing: Patient reports mild exertional shortness of breath only; no distress noted via teleconsult.
- Mental status: Alert and oriented; reports fatigue but no confusion or dizziness.
- Vitals and physical exam: Not recorded (telehealth visit).
- Accompaniment: Patient alone during consultation.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Viral upper respiratory tract infection (common cold vs. early influenza/COVID-19) without current airway compromise.
  Evidence: Sequential symptom pattern (sore throat → rhinorrhea/congestion → dry cough), low-grade fever responding to OTC medication, exposure to ill coworker, mild course, improving sore throat.
- DDx reference (aligned with DDx engine):
  1. Viral upper respiratory tract infection – High likelihood; classic progression, mild systemic features; duration 4 days.  
  2. Influenza – Moderate likelihood; systemic symptoms (myalgias, night sweats); fever resolving quickly (opposing evidence: short fever course).  
  3. Mild COVID-19 – Moderate likelihood; overlapping symptoms incl. night sweats/exertional dyspnea; no anosmia/taste loss reported and symptoms improving (opposing evidence).  
  No features supporting bacterial pharyngitis or acute airway edema.

Plan:
- Immediate actions/advice:
  • Supportive care: Rest, adequate hydration, continue paracetamol and/or ibuprofen as needed for fever/pain (advise maximum daily doses).  
  • Sick leave: Recommend 1–2 days off work to recover and limit exposure to colleagues.  
- Monitoring and red-flags:
  • If high fever (>101 °F/38.3 °C), worsening cough or shortness of breath at rest, chest pain, difficulty swallowing, voice change, stridor, or any facial/throat swelling develop, seek urgent medical evaluation or call EMS.  
- Follow-up:
  • Re-evaluate in 5–7 days if symptoms persist or worsen.  
  • Consider COVID-19 testing per local guidelines if symptoms persist or known exposure confirmed.  
  • If cough lasts >3 weeks, schedule in-office assessment and chest examination.  
  • Encourage influenza and COVID-19 vaccinations if not up to date (not discussed today).  
- Patient agreed to plan and verbalized understanding.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements: vitals, oropharyngeal examination, COVID-19 test/vaccine status, dosing specifics for OTC medications, documentation of anosmia/ageusia, confirmation of up-to-date immunizations, workplace sick note if needed.  
● Transcript/DDx conflicts: None identified.  
● Transcript quality: Clear telehealth audio; no major gaps/inaudible sections.
